proposals.before: Later he also said that Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery's father had died by violence and should not be kept close.
proposals.after: Later he also said that the Prince of Zhao Commandery, whose father had died by violence, should not be kept close.
proposals.reason: Chinese 趙郡王父死非命，不可親 warns against keeping the prince close because of his father's violent death; the idiomatic English can be read as advising distance from the already-dead father, and it inserts the given name Rui absent from this sentence.

proposals.before: Wenxiang had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian; Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan; Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning; Prince Changgong of Lanling could not obtain his mother's surname; Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.
proposals.after: Wenxiang had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian; Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan; Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning; Prince Changgong of Lanling’s mother’s surname could not be learned; Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.
proposals.reason: 不得母氏姓 means the mother’s surname was unavailable, not that Changgong personally failed to obtain it; ‘could not obtain’ makes Changgong the agent.

proposals.before: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinyang to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.
proposals.after: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinzhou to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.
proposals.reason: Chinese 晉州 is Jinzhou, not Jinyang (晉陽); both English fields substitute the wrong place-name.

proposals.before: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinyang to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.
proposals.after: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinzhou to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.
proposals.reason: Chinese 晉州 is Jinzhou, not Jinyang (晉陽); the literal English repeats the same error.

proposals.before: A Qi turncoat, Qi Fulinghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.
proposals.after: A Qi turncoat, Qifu Linghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.
proposals.reason: The surname is 乞扶 (Qifu), not Qi; 齊 marks the turncoat's former polity. Qi Fulinghe fuses the ethnonym with the personal name.

proposals.before: A Qi turncoat, Qi Fulinghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.
proposals.after: A Qi turncoat, Qifu Linghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.

proposals.after: When he reached Chang'an, by precedent he was appointed Opener of an Office (kaifu) and Marquis of a county.
proposals.reason: 開府 is kaifu, opening a headquarters with staff, not 'Opener of the Way'.

proposals.after: While governor of Ying Province, the acting adjutant Yang Shishen submitted a detailed list of his corruption, and he was dismissed.
proposals.reason: 陽士深 is the personal name Yang Shishen; 表列 is the verb 'to list in a memorial,' not part of the name Shibiao.

proposals.after: At first, while in Ying Province, the acting adjutant Yang Shishen submitted a detailed list of his corrupt acts, and he was dismissed from office.

proposals.after: During the campaign against Dingyang, Shishen was with the army and feared retribution.
proposals.reason: 士深 is the given name of Yang Shishen already named in the previous sentence, not a separate person Shi Shen.

proposals.after: When they campaigned against Dingyang, Shishen was with the army, fearing that retribution would reach him.

proposals.after: He then found a minor fault, had Shishen beaten twenty strokes, and put the matter to rest.

proposals.after: He then found a minor fault, had Shishen beaten twenty strokes, and so reassured him.

proposals.after: At the battle of Pingyang, Houzhu personally took command, ordering Yanzong to lead the right wing in the first attack; below the walls they captured Zhou's Opening-Office General Zong Ting.
